issue_context.summary: Explorer can retain thumbnails generated by a PowerToys provider after the provider is disabled or uninstalled because the shell cache outlives registration changes.
known_information: The issue arose while validating preview/thumbnail enable-disable behavior.
Manual thumbnail cache cleanup consistently removed stale entries.
Windows documentation recommends SHChangeNotify with SHCNE_ASSOCCHANGED when handlers are registered.
inferences: Extension-specific deletion of all existing cached thumbnails is not exposed as a reliable supported operation.
issue_context.analysis: The code now performs the supported invalidation step. The residual user communication is already represented by the narrower open issue.

comment.body: The supported handler-refresh work from this issue was implemented in merged PR #12996, and current File Explorer add-on code calls `SHChangeNotify(SHCNE_ASSOCCHANGED)` after applying or removing registrations. Windows can still retain thumbnails that were already generated, and the remaining user-facing warning/cleanup guidance is tracked in #13618. I suggest closing this broader issue as handled by those two items.

title: [File Explorer] Disabling/uninstalling thumbnail providers may require cleaning up the thumbnail cache
